rules.rationale: ML-DSA provides compact lattice-based digital signatures with high-speed verification, standard for authentication and PKI.

tradeoffs.signature_size: ML-DSA-65 signature is 3,309 bytes (vs 256 bytes for RSA-2048 and 64 bytes for ECDSA P-256).
tradeoffs.consideration: Inspect protocol message buffers and database column sizes to accommodate multi-kilobyte signatures.

rules.rationale: ML-KEM delivers sub-millisecond lattice-based key encapsulation to counter Store-Now-Decrypt-Later threats.

tradeoffs.consideration: Use hybrid mode (X25519 + ML-KEM-768) during transition phase to preserve FIPS 140-3 compliance while gaining quantum security.

rules.alternative_pqc: AES-256-GCM with pre-shared quantum key distribution / KDF
rules.rationale: PQC does not directly provide trapdoor one-way asymmetric encryption like RSA-OAEP; modern architectures encapsulate a symmetric session key with ML-KEM and encrypt payload with AES-256-GCM.

tradeoffs.architecture_shift: Requires transition from direct public-key encryption to hybrid KEM-DEM (Key/Data Encapsulation Mechanism) envelope.
tradeoffs.consideration: Payloads remain AES-speed; only key header grows by ~1.1 KB.

rules.rationale: Symmetric ciphers are not broken by Shor's algorithm, but Grover's search halves effective security. Upgrading key size to 256 bits guarantees 128-bit quantum security.

tradeoffs.performance: Negligible on modern CPUs with AES-NI instructions.
tradeoffs.consideration: Key storage and key management systems must support 256-bit keys.

rules.rationale: Immediate hygiene upgrade required. MD5 and SHA-1 have classical collision vulnerabilities.

tradeoffs.consideration: Verify digest length compatibility in calling modules.

rules.alternative_pqc: IPSec / WireGuard with pre-shared PQC secrets
rules.rationale: Protects transport data against passive recording and retrospective decryption.

tradeoffs.handshake_size: ClientHello and ServerHello increase by ~1.2 KB.
tradeoffs.consideration: Ensure network middleboxes and firewalls do not drop enlarged handshake packets.

rules.rationale: Dual-signature certificates allow legacy systems to validate ECDSA while quantum-aware systems validate ML-DSA, ensuring backward compatibility.

tradeoffs.cert_size: Certificate size increases from ~1.5 KB to ~5 KB.
tradeoffs.consideration: CA root and intermediate hierarchy must support composite OIDs.
